hints: Look closely at the structure and notice the three -OH groups are not all the same type.
Malic acid has two $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ carboxylic acid groups and one alcohol $\text{-OH}$ group on the middle carbon.
Think about which reagent is strong enough to remove H from both strong carboxylic acids and the very weak alcohol group to give hydrogen gas.
walkthrough:
**Identify the three -OH groups**

Malic acid is not a tri-carboxylic acid. It has two different functional groups.

Count them as: $2 \times \text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ (carboxylic acid) + $1 \times \text{-OH}$ (secondary alcohol).

**Recall acid strength difference**

Carboxylic acid $\text{-OH}$ is fairly acidic and reacts with bases and metals. Alcohol $\text{-OH}$ is very weakly acidic.

$$\text{RCO}_2\text{H} \text{ is a much stronger acid than } \text{ROH}$$

**Test each reagent type**

Esterification, alkalis like KOH, and carbonates only attack the acidic carboxylic groups, not the alcohol.

Only a very reactive metal like sodium reacts with both types:
$$2\text{ROH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RONa} + \text{H}_2$$
$$2\text{RCO}_2\text{H} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RCO}_2\text{Na} + \text{H}_2$$

**Conclude the answer**

So 1 mole of malic acid will use 3 moles of Na atoms to react with all three -OH groups and release $1.5$ moles of $\text{H}_2$. This matches the reagent that reacts with everything.

options.A: Ethanol with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ causes esterification of carboxylic acids only. It will esterify the two $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ groups but will not react with the secondary alcohol -OH in this way, so only two groups react.
options.B: Potassium hydroxide, KOH, is a strong alkali that neutralises acids. It will neutralise the two carboxylic acid groups to form salts plus water, but the alcohol -OH is too weakly acidic to react with aqueous hydroxide, so only two groups react.
options.C: Sodium metal is reactive enough to oxidise both carboxylic acids and alcohols. It reacts with the two $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ groups and also with the alcohol $\text{-OH}$ group, giving $\text{-ONa}$ and $\text{-CO}_2\text{Na}$ salts plus $\text{H}_2$ gas. All three -OH groups react.
options.D: Sodium carbonate, $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$, is a weak base. It is basic enough to react with carboxylic acids to give salt, water and $\text{CO}_2$, but not basic enough to react with an alcohol. So only the two $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ groups react.
